groups.label: Matrix, diagnostics and generic flipper positions
groups.notes: Sequential matrix numbering: public = 8 * zero-based strobe + zero-based return + 1. The shared by35.c reader can select six columns; a five-column machine fits only 1-40. Self test -7 drives PIA0 CA1, CPU diagnostic -6 drives NMI, and sound diagnostic -5 calls the selected sound board; a chime-only game has no sound board to receive it. GEN_STMPU100 uses the Bally-style cabinet port (coins 9-11, credit 6, tilt 7, slam 16), unlike GEN_STMPU200. Those port writes occur only with keyboard handling enabled. The row read is uncomplemented, the generation does not select BY35HW_REVSW, and the game supplies any inversion mask. Consume public state as delivered. The generic flipper column publishes 81-88; lower buttons are right 82 and left 84. FLIP_SW without FLIP_SWNO does not copy them into the ROM matrix, but core_updateSw still uses the lower button bits to synthesize flipper outputs. The driver cannot select the generic flipper column in its row reader. Availability and physical fitment are game-specific.

groups.label: MPU option switches S1-S32
groups.notes: Four eight-switch banks. Public ordinal N is bank floor((N-1)/8), bit (N-1)%8. GEN_STMPU100 selects BY35HW_DIP4. These are configuration switches, independent of identically numbered playfield inputs.

groups.label: Physical flipper end-of-stroke contacts
groups.notes: Profile-local identities 1 left and 2 right are winding-bypass contacts outside PinMAME's switch API. The machine establishes construction, quantity and geometry.

groups.label: Momentary, continuous and synthetic flipper outputs
groups.notes: PIA1 B selector 0-14 publishes momentary address selector+1; selector 15 is masked off, so 16 is unreachable. The inverted high nibble publishes continuous 17-20. core_updateSw is enabled by public 19. Cabinet-wired flippers synthesize right 45/46 and left 47/48 together for the full enabled lower-button closure, without physical winding or EOS timing. Tables normally consume 46/48. An address with a meaningful duplicate state is used, even if it has no separate physical load. Printed coil-test numbers and transistor numbers require the game's own mapping.

groups.label: Main-board discrete SCR lamp outputs
groups.notes: Main-board public = 16 * lamp-data-line + decoder selector + 1, selectors 0-14. Slots 16,32,48,64 are unreachable; public 15 is valid. The lamp driver has sixty discrete SCRs, not a switch-style matrix. Trace each decoder line through the game's own resistor/SCR and connector drawing; SCR numbers are not public addresses. This profile covers the main board; auxiliary hardware requires a separately reviewed profile.

groups.label: Transformer-fed general illumination
groups.notes: Physical identity 1 denotes uncontrolled G.I. when established by the machine's wiring. It has no PinMAME callback. The machine supplies its circuits, regions and socket evidence.
